#Text Extractor

This notebook takes a large block of text from Proquest, containing 500 peer-reviewed articles, and extracts them to individual text files and builds a dataframe.

Extract the full text of each ProQuest article into its own .txt file
Each article starts with a line of underscores followed by "Document X of 500". For every article, the text from "Full text:" up to
(but not including) "Subject:" is saved to extracted_articles/<headline>.txt

You begin by putting the ProQuest article data into the "source_demo" folder. 
It must be in raw text format and have a .txt extension.

This is based on 2019 code developed by Austin Wilkins and Rob Wells for a project investigating media coverage of Chinese companies.
It has been streamlined and modified by Google Gemini 3, Oct 27 2026.

#streamlined

# Function 1 - Safe Filename, Clean filenames so they don't break 
```{r}

safe_filename <- function(x, max_chars = 150) {
  x %>%
    str_replace_all('[\\\\/:*?"<>|\\r\\n\\t]', " ") %>%
    str_squish() %>%
    str_sub(1, max_chars) %>%
    str_remove("[ .]+$")
}
```


#Function 2 - Extract a single article from text lines
```{r}


extract_one <- function(lines) {
  doc_idx <- str_which(lines, "^\\s*Document \\d+ of \\d+")[1]
  if (is.na(doc_idx)) return(NULL)
  
  doc_num <- as.integer(str_match(lines[doc_idx], "Document (\\d+) of")[, 2])

  title_idx <- str_which(lines, "^Title:\\s*")[1]
  headline <- if (!is.na(title_idx)) {
    str_remove(lines[title_idx], "^Title:\\s*")
  } else {
    after <- tail(lines, -doc_idx)
    after[str_trim(after) != ""][1]
  }
  headline <- str_squish(headline)

  year_idx <- str_which(lines, "^Publication year:\\s*")[1]
  year <- if (is.na(year_idx)) NA_character_ else {
    str_squish(str_remove(lines[year_idx], "^Publication year:\\s*"))
  }

  ft_start <- str_which(lines, regex("^Full text:", ignore_case = TRUE))[1]
  if (is.na(ft_start)) {
    return(tibble(article_nmbr = doc_num, Year = year, headline = headline,
                  status = "no full text", body = list(NULL)))
  }

  subj <- str_which(lines, regex("^Subject:", ignore_case = TRUE))
  ft_end <- subj[subj > ft_start][1]
  status <- "ok"
  
  if (is.na(ft_end)) {
    ft_end <- length(lines) + 1
    status <- "ok (no Subject: line, took text to end of article)"
  }

  body <- lines[ft_start:(ft_end - 1)]
  body[1] <- str_remove(body[1], regex("^Full text:\\s*", ignore_case = TRUE))

  keep <- which(str_trim(body) != "")
  body <- if (length(keep)) body[min(keep):max(keep)] else character(0)

  tibble(article_nmbr = doc_num, Year = year, headline = headline,
         status = status, body = list(body))
}

```

#Function 3 - Process text File, core processor for any given text file
```{r}

process_text_file <- function(file_path, out_dir) {
  TEXT <- tibble(Text = read_lines(file_path)) %>%
    mutate(Text = str_remove(Text, "\\s+$"),
           is_sep = str_detect(Text, "^_{20,}$"),
           newarticle = cumsum(is_sep)) %>%
    filter(newarticle > 0, !is_sep)
#Function 2 - Extract a single article from text lines
  TEXT %>%
    group_split(newarticle) %>%
    map_dfr(~ extract_one(.x$Text))
}
```

#Function 4 - Master wrapper: handles single files or entire folders automatically
Name your input and output directories here: 
input is "source_demo"
output is "extracted_demo"

```{r}
make_TidyTexts <- function(target = "source_demo", out_dir = "extracted_demo") {
  dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

  # Determine if target is a specific file or a folder to batch-process
  files <- if (dir.exists(target)) {
    list.files(path = target, pattern = "\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE)
  } else if (file.exists(target)) {
    target
  } else {
    stop("Target '", target, "' is neither a valid file nor directory.")
  }

  if (length(files) == 0) stop("No .txt files found to process.")

  # Process all target files and bind results
  #Function 3 - Process text File
  all_articles <- map_dfr(files, function(f) {
    message("Processing: ", basename(f))
    process_text_file(f, out_dir) %>% mutate(source_file = basename(f))
  })

  # Function 1 - Safe Filename, Clean filenames so they don't break 
  # Handle duplicate headlines & assign unique safe filenames cleanly
  all_articles <- all_articles %>%
    mutate(
      file_base = safe_filename(headline),
      file_base = if_else(is.na(file_base) | file_base == "", paste("Document", article_nmbr), file_base)
    ) %>%
    group_by(file_base) %>%
    mutate(file_base = if (n() > 1) paste0(file_base, " (Doc ", article_nmbr, ")") else file_base) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(file = if_else(str_starts(status, "ok"), file.path(out_dir, paste0(file_base, ".txt")), NA_character_))

  # Write out valid article text files
  to_write <- all_articles %>% filter(!is.na(file))
  walk2(to_write$body, to_write$file, ~ write_lines(.x, .y))

  # Build and save index
  index <- all_articles %>%
    mutate(n_lines = map_int(body, length)) %>%
    select(source_file, article_nmbr, Year, headline, file, status, n_lines)

  index_name = if (dir.exists(target)) "_master_index.csv" else paste0("_index_", sub("\\.txt$", "", basename(target)), ".csv")
  index_path <- file.path(out_dir, index_name)
  write_csv(index, index_path)

  message("\nDone! ", sum(str_starts(index$status, "ok")), " of ", nrow(index), 
          " articles written to ", out_dir, "/ (Index saved as ", index_name, ")")

  invisible(index)
}
```

# Execute the code
```{r}
index <- make_TidyTexts("source_demo")
```
